strings.name: António Guterres
strings.role: UN secretary-general · Former Portuguese prime minister
strings.summary: Guterres moved from engineering into Portugal’s parliament and government, serving as prime minister from 1995 to 2002 before leading UNHCR. He became UN secretary-general in 2017 and promoted climate action, sustainable development and conflict mediation. Divisions among member states and Security Council deadlock constrain this work. His remarks on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict also prompted diplomatic controversy, illustrating the tensions between advocacy and political limits.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: A former Portuguese prime minister and UN refugee-agency chief, he advanced peace, climate and development agendas as UN secretary-general.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Leading refugee protection
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led UNHCR from 2005 to 2015, pursuing organizational reform and responding to large displacement crises.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Advancing multilateral agendas
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: As secretary-general, promoted climate action, development goals and peace diplomacy.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Addressed the climate summit
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Addressed the COP31 Leaders’ Summit in Antalya and continued to press for climate action.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Controversy over Israel-Palestine remarks
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Israeli officials criticized his discussion of the conflict’s context; he reiterated his condemnation of Hamas attacks and denied justifying them.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Appointed to a second term
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The General Assembly appointed him for a second term running from January 2022 to December 2026.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Began as UN secretary-general
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Succeeded Ban Ki-moon as the ninth secretary-general after his 2016 appointment by the General Assembly.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became high commissioner for refugees
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Led UNHCR as high commissioner until the end of 2015.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Left the premiership
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Resigned after the Socialist Party’s losses in the 2001 local elections and subsequently left the premiership.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became Portuguese prime minister
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Led the Socialist Party to an election victory and another win in 1999.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Elected to parliament
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Entered Portugal’s parliament after democratization and worked on social and governance issues.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completed engineering studies
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduated from Instituto Superior Técnico in Lisbon and briefly worked in teaching.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Lisbon
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born and raised in Portugal’s capital.
